body:
### Problem

Regarding smart indent, it has specific behaviour when working with curly bracket languages (e.g. CSS). It has a different behaviour depending on if you already have a curly closing bracket AFTER the cursor. It either adds indentation or not. This behaviour seems to be consistent with CSS, SCSS, Javascript, and also these languages nested inside a Astro file.

However, when working with a Svelte file, it behaves differently. Inside a svelte file, it always adds an indent. I have discovered this while using a plugin which has keymaps relying on the indent behaviour. The difference sounds minimal, but has soon as something is automated inside a keymap or a macro, it becomes significant.

During my investigation, I've realised that inside Neovim there is an `indent` directory with a file for Astro, but not one for Svelte. If I install it in my own `.config/nvim/indent` by copying the Astro file and renaming it, it works fine. It has a few other quirks that I can report, but it fixes the issue I am talking about here.

Now I've discussed this with @echasnovski because he helped me investigate this and he mentioned that these indent files might be copied verbatim from Vim itself. So I am not sure how much Neovim can deviate from Vim for this matter or if it is better to report this on the `Vim` repo itself. I get the same problem. At least with Vim 9.1.

At this point, my thinking is that since there is no Svelte specific indent file, and since I can reproduce it with a `--clean` start, it seems like it still depends on some kind of default behaviour that should be fixed. Something that makes the indenting work differently in a file with nested languages until it is patched with an indent file. 

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
nvim --clean
```

Then

```vim
:set autoindent
:set smartindent
:set ft=svelte
```

Then try with and without a closing curly after the cursor.

```html
<style>
section {|
</style>
```

Pressing `<CR>` will do:

```html
<style>
section {
        |
</style>
```

And with the closing curly bracket AFTER the cursor.

```html
<style>
section {|}
</style>
```

Pressing `<CR>` will do:

```html
<style>
section {
        |}
</style>
```


### Expected behavior

This last case is not the regular behaviour in a pure CSS/SCSS file. Or even a Javascript, and an HTML file or an Astro file. When there is a closing curly bracket after the cursor, it should not indent and align with `section {` since this is how it behaves in other file types. 

The Astro file behaves exactly like in an HTML file. As in, it also enforces the indent inside the style tag.

```html
<style>
        section {
        |}
</style>
```

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

v0.12.6

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

yes, Vim 9.1

### Operating system/version

macOS 27.0.1

### Terminal name/version

Ghostty 1.4.0

### $TERM environment variable

tmux-256color

### Installation

Homebrew
